procurement_notes: Must buy via AWS Marketplace for vendor onboarding + PO workflow. Legal prefers public offer unless discount requires private offer; wants standard terms + clear refund/credit policy.
use_case_and_requirements_summary: Media/ads team building internal campaign assistant + creative variant generator. Heavy focus on unit economics: wants predictable cost per 1k requests and guardrails for runaway token usage. Workload split: ~70% chat-style generation (short outputs, high QPS bursts during campaign launches), ~30% embeddings/classification (brand safety + dedupe). Interested in Hosted API first; Dedicated only if latency variance is high during peak season.
performance_requirements: Latency target: p95 < 700ms for short chat (<=250 output tokens) at steady state; tolerates p95 1.2s during burst. Throughput target: 150-300 RPS bursts for 10-20 min windows. Needs streaming for UI. Wants autoscaling behavior explained (even if Hosted) and guidance on client-side retries/backoff.
cost_controls_requirements: Wants hard limits by org/project: max tokens/day, max spend/day; alerting when nearing limits; dashboard breaking down cost by route/model; recommendation to use caching/batching where applicable. Asked specifically for: 'Can we cap output tokens per request and prevent prompt bloat?'
model_and_routing_notes: No strict model pinning initially; wants 1-2 Redwood-verified open models for copy generation and an embeddings model for classification. Asked about fallback behavior: if region capacity constrained, prefer cross-region fallback over hard failure, but needs audit trail of which model/region served the request.
security_and_compliance_notes: Security team asked for SOC 2 report availability (on request), encryption at rest/in transit details, and whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys (KMS). Audit logs required for org admin actions + API key lifecycle; export to SIEM is 'nice to have' but not blocker for pilot. Retention: prefers minimal retention of prompts/outputs; asked if request/response logging can be disabled while keeping operational metrics.
onboarding_friction_notes: Multiple points of confusion during Marketplace path: (1) After AWS subscription, console still showed 'No entitlement found' for ~35 min; user retried and created duplicate org by accident. (2) Docs: they followed generic quickstart (non-marketplace) and got stuck on billing step. (3) Metering: finance saw unfamiliar dimension name in AWS console and escalated internally. Requested a single step-by-step 'Marketplace → entitlement → org linking → first API key → verify metering' page and clearer error text with retry guidance.
